title: paint-by-words: goal-conditioned intervention retrieval from a Cell Painting archive, with calibrated refusal
description:
Ask a cell-image archive for a phenotype in plain English. Get a compound, a dose and the evidence, or a refusal. Built on RxRx3-core (Recursion), which is not redistributed here.

The repository includes the paper Most of It Was Toxicity, which reports a measurement artefact affecting per-cell morphological features: they are averaged over the cells that can be segmented, which are the survivors, and a dying cell reads brighter per unit area. Against a 3.5% base rate of cell loss, 64% to 69% of wells satisfying a per-cell "brighter" predicate had also lost their cells. A baseline built from the model's own prediction for "kill most of the cells", which never reads the request, scored AUC 0.833 where the model scored 0.842; redefining each predicate to require surviving cells lowers the headline to 0.799 and raises the margin tenfold. The same confound recurs in LINCS L1000 transcriptomics as nonspecific transcriptional response.

Ships the evaluation protocol with both trivial baselines printed beside every number, calibrated refusal, dose windows, the exact prompt used for the vision-language branch, 30 tests, and one command that regenerates every figure and number.
